text:
Ms Samantha Bruin 
Senior Nurse
Greywall Nursing Home
27 Station Road
Greywalls

05/01/2018

Dear Ms Bruin,

Re: Mr Gerald Baker, aged 79

I am writing to refer Mr Baker, who was admitted to our hospital for a left total hip replacement on his left side as a result of osteoarthritis. He is due to be discharged back to your care today.

After the surgery, Mr. Baker has experienced possibly postoperative disorientation to time and place, as well as an episode of anemia, which was treated by a PRBC blood transfusion. Both conditions are resolved now; however, a continued observation is recommended and follow-up blood tests are arranged at our clinic. Apart from those, he has made good progress with good mobility using a wheelie-walker.

Mr. Baker has been placed on 100mg of Aspirin daily after surgery, and Panadenie Forte as needed for surgical pain. In addition, he is on Ramipril 5 mg daily for hypertension. 

Please note that Mr. Baker’s surgical incision site needs to be dressed daily, and the staples will be removed in two weeks. Regarding his mobility, please ensure that he follows his exercise program. As we will provide him with a hired wheelie-walker and a wedge pillow for 2 weeks, please prepare him a toilet raiser for now.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,
RN

(202W)

Mr. Gerald Baker is a 79-year-old patient on the ward of a hospital in which you are Charge nurse.

Patient’s Details:
Marital status:    Widower (8 years)
Admission dates:  3 September 2010 (City Hospital)
Discharge dates:  7 September 2010
Diagnosis:       Left Total Hip Replacement (THR)
               Ongoing high blood pressure

Social background: Lives at Greywalls Nursing Home (GNH)(4 years)
                No children
                Employed as a radio engineer until retirement aged 65
                Now aged-pensioner
                Hobbies: chess, Ham radio operator
                Sister, Dawn Mason (66), Visits regularly; v supportive
                -plays chess with Mr. Baker on her visits
                No sign of dementia observed

Medical background:  2008- osteoarthritis requiring total hip replacement surgery
                   1989- Hypertension (ongoing management)
                   1985-Colles Fracture (ORIF)

Medications:  Aspirin 100 mg mane(recommended post-operatively )
             Ramipril 5mg mane
             Panadeine Forte (co-codamol) 2 qid prn

Nursing management and progress:
             Daily dressings surgery incision site
             Range of motion, stretching and strengthening exercises
             Occupational therapy
             Staples to be removed in two wks (21/9)
             Also, follow –up FBE and UAE tests at City Hospital Clinic

Assessment: 
Good mobility post –operation
Weight-bearing with use of wheelie-walker; walks length of ward without difficulty
Post-operative disorientation re time and place during recovery, possibly relating to anesthetic- continued observation recommended 
Dropped Hb post-operatively (to 72), requiring transfusion of 3 units packed red blood cells; Hb stabled (112) on discharge- ongoing monitoring required for anaemia.

Discharge plan:  Monitor medications (Panadeine Forte)
              Preserve skin integrity
              Continue exercise program
              Equipment required: wheelie-walker, wedge pillow, toilet raiser
               Hospital to provide walker and pillow. Hospital social worker organized 2-wk hire of raiser from local medical supplier.

Writing task:
Using the information in the case notes, write a letter to Ms Samantha Bruin, Senior Nurse at Greywalls Nursing Home, 27 Station Road, Greywalls, who will be responsible for Mr. Baker's continued care at the Nursing Home.

In your answer:
. expand the relevant notes into complete sentences
. do not use note form
. use letter format
The body of the letter should be approximately 180-200 words.
